solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charlie at match in one-piece garment

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to match is to suit, as colours that go together

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie turns up to a sports match wearing an all-in-one outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting all-in-one bodysuit covering torso and legs is a single-piece item of clothing.

clue.text: Large firm's constant, terribly poor quota

parts.note: c is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the word poor are badly messed up and rearranged

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A big company is criticised for its fixed rules and a miserable allocation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Large firm' is a link word meaning 'has', and 'terribly' is the anagram signal acting on 'poor' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation is a big company or business organisation, a legal entity trading at scale.

clue.text: Creeping plant in house on wheels

definitions.meaning: a plant that trails along the ground or hangs down, as ivy may
a caravan or mobile home towed behind a car

explanation.surface: A climbing plant has crept into a caravan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sprawling plant that trails over the ground and a towed caravan or mobile home.

clue.text: Mad route taken by Ivy climbing?

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for furious or crazed
ivy grows upward along a wall, so read literally the phrase traces its path

explanation.surface: Someone named Ivy, climbing, takes a crazy route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' is capitalised to look like a person's name; it is the plant, which climbs walls. The question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means driven to distraction or crazy, while literally describing a climb up a vertical surface.

clue.text: Seeing upper-class in streetcar, a shock

indicators.note: in tells us the upper-class letter sits within the vehicle word

parts.note: streetcar is the American word for a tram

explanation.surface: A posh passenger on a streetcar experiences a nasty jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a severe emotional or physical shock, the lasting harm from a distressing event.

clue.text: Top dog heard

indicators.note: heard means the word for the dog is spoken aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a Peke is a Pekinese, a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: The best hound has been listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the summit or highest point, so it means the top of something.

clue.text: Normal soldier? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite tells us the soldier word falls short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a parachute soldier

explanation.surface: A not entirely ordinary soldier is asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard or average level, so below par means worse than usual.

clue.text: Horrify a missionary in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives a word spelt differently

parts.note: St Paul was the great missionary of the early Church, so a missionary is a Paul

explanation.surface: A preacher is shocked by what is said to him.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror or dismay, the same as to shock someone deeply.

clue.text: Take it on ahead of performance

indicators.note: ahead of places the word for on in front of the performance word

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
an act is a performance, as on stage

explanation.surface: An actor is urged to accept a role before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something in a certain way is to respond to it, as in how did she take the news.

clue.text: America's initial support, very large by the way

indicators.note: initial picks out the opening letter of the word for America

parts.note: a prop is something that holds another thing up
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very large

explanation.surface: The US gives early backing that is huge, incidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used alone, introduces a remark that is incidental, as in incidentally.

clue.text: Why a player's unable to go on?

definitions.text: Why a player's unable to go on?

parts.words: Why a player's unable to go on?
parts.note: it looks like a sports player injured; the player is an actor too nervous to go on stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests sport and 'go on' suggests continuing; here an actor freezes before entering the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage fright is nervousness before performing that can stop an actor appearing in front of an audience.

clue.text: Hooter in stadium leader's blown

indicators.note: blown means lost, so the leading letter of the stadium word is gone

parts.note: a bowl is a stadium, especially in American usage, such as the Rose Bowl

explanation.surface: A horn sounds in a stadium as the front-runner wastes his lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like a horn or a nose; it is the bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooter is a nocturnal bird of prey, named for its call.

clue.text: Hugo's girl's gem about small article

indicators.note: about means the gem word goes around the small letter

parts.note: an emerald is a green precious stone
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl owned a jewel concerning a minor item.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the gypsy heroine of Victor Hugo's novel The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Well thought of agent on university board

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the agent word sits above the rest

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A respected agent sits on a university's governing board.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reputable has a good reputation and is held in high regard.

clue.text: A plain in a foreign land

parts.note: broad means plain or clear, as in a broad hint

explanation.surface: A flat expanse in some faraway country.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means overseas, in or to another country.

clue.text: Meagre sum originally held in reserve

indicators.note: held in means the first letter of sum is kept inside the reserve word

parts.note: spare means extra or kept in reserve, as a spare tyre

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of sum

explanation.surface: A paltry amount was first kept back as a reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty, so scant and meagre in quantity.

clue.text: Express great happiness about Irish writer on the radio

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: on the radio means the writer's name is broadcast, so only its sound counts

parts.note: James Joyce was the Irish author of Ulysses

explanation.surface: A broadcast about an Irish author brings joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy or delight.

clue.text: Expert giving support to guys in danger

indicators.note: in a down clue, support means the expert word goes underneath the guys word

parts.note: guys are men
an ace is an expert, someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: A specialist helps out some men in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat, something likely to cause harm.

clue.text: Rude about five on the rocks

indicators.note: about means the rudeness word wraps around the Roman numeral

parts.note: insolent means rude or disrespectful
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A rude remark about five people drinking whisky on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests a drink over ice; here it means in financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing, unable to pay its debts, which is bankrupt.

clue.text: Impish youngster having most of shellfish

indicators.note: most of means the shellfish word loses its last letter

parts.note: scampi are large prawns, Norway lobsters

explanation.surface: A cheeky child eats most of the seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, especially a playful child.

clue.text: Jack having a drop of rum, and glass of beer

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

indicators.note: a drop of means only a tiny amount, the first letter of rum

explanation.surface: Jack has some rum, then a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is British slang for a glass of beer, as in going for a jar at the pub.

clue.text: Once more, in retreat, artist falls

indicators.note: in retreat means the phrase meaning once more goes backwards

parts.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist falls back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Simple tune from Hairspray

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A catchy melody comes from the musical Hairspray.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody, a simple song or tune.

clue.text: Fetch bishop round

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a ring is a round shape, a circle

explanation.surface: Go and get the bishop to come over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to fetch it, carrying it here.

clue.text: Turn down short branch line

indicators.note: short means the rejecting word lacks its last letter

parts.note: to spurn is to reject or turn down

explanation.surface: A short railway branch is refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a short railway line or road branching off a main route.

clue.text: Factor in a small amount

definitions.meaning: a trace, as in an ... of truth

explanation.surface: Something counts as a factor, though only in a small way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a constituent part and a slight trace, as in an element of doubt.
